newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ sees NZ c/a deficit peaking at 5.9 pct/GDP.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ sees NZ c/a deficit peaking at 5.9 pct/GDP.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand forecast in its six monthly Monetary Policy Statement published on Friday that New Zealand's current account account deficit would peak at 5.9 percent of GDP in the year to March 1998.
From that level, the deficit ratio is seen falling to 5.4 percent in 1999 and 4.8 percent in 2000.

In the bank's previous forecasts published in March, the bank saw the deficit peaking at 6.0 percent in 1999 and Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash said then that the magnitude of such a deficit was unsustainable.

On Friday, the RBNZ said that from 1998 the outlook for the tradeable sector improved as firms responded to a mild stimulus from international demand and the gradual depreciation of the real exchange rate over the projection period.

"The improved outlook for export growth, along with a reversal of recent declines in the terms of trade, strengthens the trade balance and eases the pressure on the current account deficit, which we project to be just below five percent of GDP by the turn of the century," the bank said.
